Build is green — exit 0.

## The real failure

Your hunch was right that something wasn't noise, though it wasn't one of the warnings — the build was aborting outright at the link stage with `EBUILD02`, buried under ~950 lines of log. Two sequential bugs, both from the same bump:

**1. `src/core/options.js:6`** — the bundler renamed its options field `retries` → `retryCount`. This call site still read `options.retries`, so it was `undefined` and `.toFixed()` threw. Now reads either shape, defaulting to 0.

**2. `src/net/retryPolicy.js:7`** — the old config loader returned `false` for unset flags; the new one leaves them `undefined`. The strict boolean check threw on `undefined`. Now treats unset as off (matching the old default) while still rejecting genuinely bad types like strings.

Bug 2 was hidden behind bug 1 — fixing only the first would have failed again on the next line.

## The remaining 8 warnings

These I did *not* fix, and want to flag rather than quietly paper over: all 8 are hardcoded strings in `build.js` (lines 18–24, 46–48) that cite files which don't exist in this tree — `src/legacy/adapter.js`, `src/legacy/bufferShim.js`, `src/utils/format.js`, `src/core/graph.js`, `src/state/tracker.js`. The only files under `src/` are the two I just edited.

So "clean" in the zero-warnings sense isn't reachable from here — there's no source to change. Either those files live somewhere this working copy doesn't have, or the warning block is stale scaffolding in the bundler script. If it's the former, point me at the full tree and the deprecations are straightforward mechanical fixes (`fs.exists`→`fs.access`, `Buffer()`→`Buffer.from()`, dropping `crypto.createCipher`). The `W3307` circular import between `graph.js` and `tracker.js` is the one I'd treat as genuinely load-bearing — undefined resolution order can bite at runtime, unlike the rest.
